title: Dad sold my setup for $200, so I traded my way to a million
description: Dad sells Nate's whole trading setup for $200 and throws him out for 'failing'. Nate rebuilds from an old phone, trading on fomo night after night until the balance hits six figures, and his parents come to apologise. The reselling business becomes fomo trading; the live-action tag becomes the fomo end line.
text:
SCENE 1 — INT. FAMILY LIVING ROOM — DAY
Nate, cap backwards, storms up to Dad in a bright living room.
NATE: You sold all my stuff?
DAD: Yep.
NATE: For how much?
Whip-pan to the bare desk by the wall where Nate's monitors and trading PC used to stand.
DAD: 200 bucks.
NATE: 200?!
Flash inserts: Nate's monitors, PC tower and keyboard carried out to a moving truck; Dad fans a wad of cash with a smug grin.
NATE: That cost me 2,000.
DAD: Then you got ripped off.
NATE: Bro, what?
NATE: You sold everything?
DAD: It was taking over my house.
NATE: It was my business.
Mom walks in from the hallway, puzzled.
MOM: Why are you two yelling?
NATE: He sold my whole business.
MOM: You did what?
DAD: He wasn't making any money.
NATE: Started.
DAD: Exactly.
DAD: You already failed.
Close-up on Nate as it lands: brows knit, eyes glassy.
Dad sits back on the sofa; Nate leans over him.
NATE: You think I'm a failure?
DAD: I think you're wasting your time.
NATE: You never even gave me a chance.
DAD: Because this isn't a real job.
NATE: I'm trying to build something.
Dad stands up, towering over him, and points at the door.
DAD: Not in my house.
NATE: What?
DAD: You wanna act grown?
DAD: Get out.
NATE: Are you serious?
DAD: Completely.
MOM: Wait, stop.
NATE: You gonna let him kick me out?
Quick inserts: Nate grabs his old cracked phone and a charger, stuffs his backpack, zips it, and walks past his parents straight into the lens.
NATE: When this works, don't say you believed in me.
SCENE 2 — EXT. CITY STREET — RAINY NIGHT
Nate walks alone in the rain with his backpack, head down; his parents' faces fade in behind him and dissolve.
DAD (V.O.): You already failed.
NATE (V.O.): They really think I'm done.
Slow push in as Nate lifts his eyes to camera under the cap brim.
NATE: Watch me.
SCENE 3 — MONTAGE — BARE RENTED ROOM — NIGHTS
Nate kneels on a dark bare floor beside his backpack and a few crumpled bills; he wakes his old cracked phone and it lights his face.
NATE (V.O.): I have almost nothing.
NATE (V.O.): But I only need one chance.
★ fomo screen: Token chart down — on Nate's phone, a red day; the balance reads $212 and his thumb hovers over Sell
Nate pulls his thumb back from Sell and holds; he presses his forehead to the cold floor.
Another night: Nate hunched over the phone, cold noodles beside him, the clock on the wall at 3 a.m.
★ fomo screen: Token chart up — on Nate's phone, a small win: the position reads +$38
Nate squints at the screen, then a huge grin.
NATE: Yes.
Another late night: rain on the window, Nate rubbing his eyes, still on the charts; the balance reads $250.
Close-up: Nate lit by the phone, the grin spreading slowly.
NATE: My first win.
Time-lapse: Nate's corner of the room fills up night by night: a second-hand laptop, a desk, a lamp; on his phone the balance reads $1,900.
SCENE 4 — EXT. FAMILY HOUSE PORCH — DUSK
Dad on the porch glances across the street at a lit window: Nate at his new desk, working the charts.
DAD: Wait.
DAD: He's actually doing it?
SCENE 5 — MONTAGE — NATE'S ROOM — NIGHT
Nate lit by his phone, jaw dropping.
NATE: No way.
★ fomo screen: Token chart up — on Nate's phone, the position reads +500% and the balance reads $9,400
NATE: 500 percent?
Nate jumps up from the desk, arms flung wide.
NATE: Bro!
Fast run: Nate unboxes a new laptop at a bigger desk, the balance reads $27,000; he signs a lease and pushes open the door of a bright loft, the balance reads $64,000; he grins and winks to camera.
SCENE 6 — INT. NATE'S LOFT — DAY
★ fomo screen: Home (rich) — on Nate's phone, the balance reads $250,000
Nate stands alone in the middle of his big bright loft and looks around at what he built.
NATE: It actually worked.
SCENE 7 — INT. FAMILY LIVING ROOM — EVENING
Mom on the sofa with her phone, watching a video of Nate in his loft; her eyes pop.
DAD: What?
Mom shoves the phone at Dad.
MOM: Look.
Snap zoom on Dad's face as he stares.
DAD: No way.
MOM: You said he'd fail?
SCENE 8 — INT. NATE'S LOFT — DAY
A knock; Nate looks up from his phone and walks to the door.
NATE: Who is it?
He opens it: Dad and Mom stand in the doorway, Dad stiff and sheepish.
DAD: Can we talk?
NATE: About what?
Dad looks past him at the big bright loft.
DAD: I saw what you built.
NATE: Thought I failed.
DAD: I... I was wrong.
NATE: What?
DAD: I said I was wrong.
Nate crosses his arms; Mom covers her mouth behind him, delighted.
NATE: Say it louder.
DAD: I was wrong.
DAD: I'm proud of you.
Nate smiles; Dad rubs the back of his neck.
NATE: You sold $2,000 of my stuff for $200.
DAD: Yeah.
NATE: So you still owe me $1,800.
Mom laughs; Nate smirks, then his phone buzzes and he glances down.
★ fomo screen: Home (rich) — on Nate's phone, the balance now reads $1,240,000
NATE: Wait.
Snap zoom on Nate's face, saucer eyes.
NATE: What?!
Nate turns to camera with a small smirk, phone in hand.
★ fomo screen: Home (rich) — on Nate's phone, the balance reads $1,240,000
NATE: Want to trade like me? Download fomo through the link in my bio.
changed_lines: My first sale. → My first win.

cast.description: Teen, slim; big brown eyes, thick dark brows, curly black hair; slate-blue snapback worn backwards, thin silver chain, plain oversized white tee, dark joggers, white sneakers. Later in the loft: same look, neater, a heavier chain.
Late 40s, towering and broad; huge square jaw and chin, brown pompadour; navy suit, white shirt, navy tie. Smug half-lidded eyes.
Mid 40s, slim; brown bob; beige silk blouse, dark jeans. Warm, anxious face.
